text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: authz failures spike in prod — increased user login 401s and console access errors. Paging oncall: @Chao (urgent). Incident ID: RWI-2026-042.

Chao (oncall): seeing ~15% 401s on /api/v1/session/verify across eu-prod and us-west. console load shows 502s for admin routes. grabbing logs.

Michaela: customers reporting login errors in dashboard. Emily, any high-touch customers impacted right now?

Emily (csm): Yes — 3 paying customers reported inability to log in; one enterprise tenant (Acme) on our SSO has people blocked. Prioritizing.

Samir: quick check — Okta status shows degraded performance on token verification endpoints (reported increased latency on introspect and jwks). okta-status-bot: https://status.okta.com/incident/abc123

Jordan (sre): I ran a quick curl against our introspect proxy:
```
curl -i -X POST "https://auth-proxy.prod.redwood.com/introspect" \\
  -d 'token=xxxx' -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded'
```
Response: 502 from okta-introspect upstream, and when it responds sometimes tokens fail signature verification (jwt verify error: "kid not found in cached JWKS"). Logs: `ERROR jwt: signature check failed (kid not in jwks)`

Chao (oncall): looks like JWKS rotation / propagation lag — tokens minted with new kid but our JWKS cache hasn't refreshed; Okta is intermittently returning 200 but with different keys. Could be rate limiting on our jwks fetches or Okta propagation.

Samir: I see elevated 429s on our jwks fetch path from 6:12Z. Our cache refresh backoff might be too aggressive.

Jordan (sre): Mitigation options:
- Force immediate JWKS refresh on all edge instances
- Enable short-term fallback to local pinned keys for enterprise tenants (risk: if key actually rotated we'll accept bad tokens)
- Route auth traffic to older okta cluster (if Okta offers) or fallback to internal session-store for console auth

Michaela: customer impact: blocked logins for web console and API auth — some internal automation also failing (deploys). Need to prioritize console access for SRE and support.

Chao (oncall): I'm going to force JWKS refresh first. Running command on prod-edge: `curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/refresh-jwks -d '{"force":true}'`

deploy-bot: Triggered job refresh-jwks-job #4789 by Chao. Job logs: starting fanout to 120 edges.

Jordan (sre): after refresh some edges got updated, but we still see token verify failures for tokens with kid "k-9b2f". Looks like Okta rotated their signing keys ~6:10Z and some regions didn't pick it up.

Chao (oncall): enabling session-store fallback for console routes so support + SRE can log in. Running feature toggle: `POST /admin/feature-toggles` payload: `{ "session_fallback": ["console","support"] }`

Michaela: Please document which customers we enable fallback for — Emily, coordinate with Acme to allow support access.

Emily (csm): contacting Acme now, telling them we have a mitigation and will follow up.

Samir: Okta replied on the incident: "Investigating JWKS propagation delays between our signing cluster and public JWKS endpoint, affecting some token verifications". They suggested clients implement resilient JWKS fallback.

Chao (oncall): I'm escalating to SRE lead for longer-term fix and pinning a safer backoff for JWKS refresh. @Jordan please start a playbook PR to reduce our jwks-cache TTL during key rotations.

Jordan (sre): Will do — creating PR: `ops/jwks-cache-ttl` with immediate rollback path. Also adding a healthcheck that compares token kid vs cached jwks and triggers a proactive refresh if mismatch > 0.1% of auth requests.

Michaela: Ops question — are tokens minted before 6:10Z still valid? We should accept them.

Jordan (sre): Yes, tokens minted with older key should verify against old kid; problem is when Okta rotates and some clients get new kid while our cache still has old set. We're seeing mismatches during the window.

Chao (oncall): Handoff in 30m. I'll keep the channel updated. If things degrade, escalate to incident commander. Next steps:
- Keep JWKS refresh running across remaining edges
- Keep session-store fallback enabled for console/support for 1 hour
- Monitor customer reports (Emily) and prepare external status update
- Create postmortem stub

Samir: Adding timeline notes and metrics to incident page. Current numbers: 12% of login attempts failing (national avg), spikes at 18% in eu-prod.

Emily (csm): Sent note to Acme support contact — they acknowledged and will use alternate SSO temporarily.

Chao (oncall): Okta status updated: issue marked as 'Identified' and mitigation in progress. If we see no improvement in 20m, we'll switch to token-cache fallback for all console routes.

deploy-bot: refresh-jwks-job #4789: 89/120 edges refreshed, 700ms avg per edge.

Jordan (sre): After additional refreshes, 401 rate dropped to ~4% over last 5m. Console 502s reduced.

Michaela: Good. Keep monitoring for 1hr and then start rollback of the session-store fallback once stable.

Chao (oncall): Handoff to @Jordan (sre) in 30m for escalations. I'll prepare incident summary for postmortem.

Jordan (sre): Taking primary. I'll keep the incident thread updated and spin up a short postmortem draft after stabilization.

incident-bot: Incident RWI-2026-042 status: "stabilized" (partial). Open actions: postmortem, jwks-cache TTL change, customer comms.

Michaela: Noted. Thanks team. :heart:
